newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Thomson Corp. names new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Thomson Corp. names new chief executive.

text.p: Canadian information and travel company Thomson Corp. on Monday named Richard Harrington, head of its Thomson Newspapers unit, to succeed long-time President and Chief Executive Michael Brown.

Harrington, 50, will take over as chief operating officer on July 1 and become president and chief executive on Jan. 1, 1998. Brown will become deputy chairman of Thomson, replacing John Tory, who remains as a director.
Stuart Garner, chief operating officer of Thomson Newspapers, will become chief executive of the Thomson newspaper unit when Harrington assumes the Thomson COO post.
Thomson Chairman Ken Thomson, son of company founder Roy Thomson, said he had no plans to retire.
Brown, 61, told the board four years ago he planned to leave at this time.
"I have had a good run of things running the business. I now feel rather like I am in Jurassic Park. I am history," Brown said in a statement.

Under Brown, Thomson was transformed from an advertising-dependent, newspaper-oriented organization into a specialized publishing and information group with a healthy cash flow. In the past decade, the company sold about 300 companies and bought 500 others.
Brown is a director at other companies in which the Thomson family has interests, including Canadian retailer Hudson's Bay Co. and Markborough Properties Inc..
Thomson is the biggest publisher of legal information in the United States since its $3.4 billion acquisition last year of West Publishing Co.

Some of its other assets include Toronto's Globe and Mail -- one of Canada's most influential newspapers -- Britain's Britannia Airways, a tour operator and the Lunn Poly string of travel agencies in Britain.
Thomson shares were up C25 cents to C$28.40 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.
